title: Client-side share-link password rule (6 chars + 1 digit) is weaker than the backend Zod minimum (8 chars), causing a submit that passes UI validation but fails server-side
description: ShareLinkModal.jsx PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY_REGEX only requires 6+ characters and one digit before enabling 'Generate Link'. trust-vault-service/src/utils/validators.ts CreateShareLinkSchema.password requires z.string().min(8). A 6 or 7 character password with a digit clears the client gate but is rejected by the server with a 400 Zod validation error, producing a confusing round-trip failure instead of being caught at entry.
preconditions: Logged in as a user with trust_vault.update
An active certification with no existing share links
steps: Open Share Link modal for an active certification and enable Password Protection
Enter password 'pass1w' (6 characters, includes a digit)
Observe that 'Generate Link' is enabled (client-side isPasswordValid() passes)
Click 'Generate Link' and inspect the network response from POST /share-links
expectedResult: Current behavior: the client allows submission, but the backend CreateShareLinkSchema rejects the request with 400 'Password must be at least 8 characters' — the toast shows a generic 'Failed to create share link' error with no client-side warning beforehand. This is a validation-parity gap that should be fixed by raising PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH to 8 client-side to match the server contract.

title: A user can assign themselves as reviewer of their own certification and later approve it — self-review is not blocked
description: GET /workflow/reviewers (trust-vault-service/src/routes/workflow.routes.ts) returns every active org user with no exclusion of the certification's createdBy. AssignReviewerModal.jsx renders this full list with no filter against entity.createdBy either. WorkflowTransitionService only verifies that the caller transitioning assigned/re_assign → under_review IS the assignee (or an org admin) — it never compares assignedTo against the entity's createdBy. A submitter can therefore assign themselves as reviewer and later self-approve.
preconditions: User A has trust_vault.create and trust_vault.approve
User A creates a draft certification (createdBy = User A)
steps: As User A, open the draft certification and click 'Assign Reviewer'
Search the reviewer list for User A's own name
Select User A as the assignee and submit
As User A, transition the certification assigned → under_review, then under_review → active with a 30+ character justification note
expectedResult: Current behavior: User A's own name appears in the reviewer picker, the self-assignment succeeds, and the same user is later able to transition the certification to 'active' as its own reviewer — no 403 is raised anywhere in the chain. This violates segregation of duties and should be fixed by excluding entity.createdBy from /workflow/reviewers (or rejecting assignedTo === createdBy server-side).

title: Only the assigned reviewer or an org admin can transition assigned/re_assign into under_review
description: Regression guard for the ownership check in WorkflowTransitionService.transition: it loads the latest assignment's workflow_entries record, compares assignedTo to the caller, and separately checks opts.callerPermissions.has('organization.admin') resolved server-side (never trusts client-supplied flags).
preconditions: Certification is in 'assigned' status with assignedTo = User B
User C is a different non-admin org member
steps: As User C, call POST /certifications/:id/transition with targetState 'under_review'
As User B (the actual assignee), repeat the same call
expectedResult: User C's request is rejected with 403 'Only the assigned reviewer or an admin can transition assigned → under_review'. User B's request succeeds and the certification status becomes 'under_review'.

title: Share link password entry is rate-limited to 5 failed attempts per 15-minute window
description: ShareLinkService.checkPwdRateLimit / recordFailedPwdAttempt use a Redis key ratelimit:share-pwd:{token}:{ip} with a 15-minute TTL and maxAttempts=5, guarding both access() and verifyPassword().
steps: From a single IP, submit 5 consecutive wrong passwords to POST /public/share/:token/verify-password
Submit a 6th attempt (still wrong, or even the correct password)
expectedResult: The 6th attempt is rejected with 429 'Too many failed password attempts. Try again later.' regardless of correctness, until the 15-minute window elapses.

title: Accessing an expired share link returns 410 Gone, not 403 Forbidden
description: ShareLinkService.access() explicitly checks new Date() > sl.expiresAt and returns statusCode 410 before any password/domain checks — distinguishing 'link no longer valid' from 'link exists but you're not authorized'.
preconditions: A share link exists with expiresAt in the past
steps: Call GET /public/share/:token/access on the expired token
expectedResult: Response status is 410 with error 'Share link has expired' — not 403 and not a generic 404.

title: Domain allow-list is enforced only via recipient-supplied email — the forgeable Referer header is never consulted
description: Regression guard: ShareLinkService.access() comment explicitly documents that a prior Referer-header check was removed because it is fully client-controlled (e.g. curl -H "Referer: https://allowed.com") and gave no real access control. Only isDomainAllowed(request.email, sl.allowedDomains) is used now.
preconditions: A share link exists with allowedDomains: ['acme.com']
steps: Call GET /public/share/:token/access with header Referer: https://acme.com and no email parameter
Call the same endpoint with email='attacker@evil.com' and the same forged Referer header
expectedResult: Both calls are rejected — the first with 428 'Email is required to access this document', the second with 403 'Access not allowed from your email domain'. The forged Referer header has no effect on the access decision in either case.

title: A revoked share link cannot be accessed even if it has not yet reached its expiry date
description: ShareLinkService.access() checks sl.isRevoked || !sl.isActive before the expiry check, returning 410. revoke() is soft-only (isRevoked flag), so this ordering is the only thing preventing a revoked-but-not-yet-expired link from still serving content.
preconditions: A share link was created with a 7-day expiry and then revoked on day 1
steps: Revoke the share link via DELETE /share-links/:id (or the ShareLinkModal 'Revoke link' action)
On day 2 (5 days before natural expiry), call GET /public/share/:token/access
expectedResult: Access is rejected with 410 'Share link has been revoked' even though expiresAt is still 5 days in the future.

title: Certification lookup by ID is scoped to the caller's organizationId — cross-org certification IDs are not resolvable
description: CertificationRepository.findLatest / findById are always called with user.organizationIdString (see ShareLinkService.create, getPublicInfo, access). A certification _id belonging to a different org must not resolve.
preconditions: Org A and Org B each have at least one certification
Valid JWT for a user in Org A
steps: As an Org A user, call GET /certifications/:id using a certification _id that belongs to Org B
Repeat for POST /share-links using Org B's certification _id as entityId
expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with 404 'Certification not found' — no title, framework, or file metadata belonging to Org B is returned in either response.

title: Certification revocation uses the same trust_vault.approve permission as a routine review approval — no dedicated 'revoke' permission gate
description: POST /certifications/:id/transition (certification.routes.ts) is a single endpoint gated by requirePermission(TRUST_VAULT_PERMISSIONS.APPROVE) regardless of targetState. Any user holding trust_vault.approve (needed just to close a routine under_review) can also revoke an active certification via the same call, since the route does not branch permission checks on targetState==='revoked'.
preconditions: User D has trust_vault.approve but is not an org admin and holds no distinct 'revoke' capability
steps: As User D, call POST /certifications/:id/transition with targetState='revoked' on an active certification not assigned to User D
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request succeeds (200) purely on the strength of trust_vault.approve — there is no separate trust_vault.revoke permission or four-eyes control distinguishing 'approve a review' from 'revoke a live certification'. Flagged for RBAC granularity remediation.
